Bail Bond Information for Salt Lake County

After booking into Salt Lake County jail, a judge typically sets bail at arraignment (often within 24–72 hours). Families often work with a licensed bail bondsman. A common commercial bond fee is about 10% of the bail amount (non-refundable). Example: $10,000 bail → roughly $1,000 premium, subject to local rules.

If the person cannot afford bail, they may request a reduction hearing or public defender.

For hearing schedules, contact the Salt Lake County court.

Visitation Rules at Salt Lake County Jail

Policies vary. Before visiting Salt Lake County Metro Jail, confirm:

  • Approved ID: Government-issued photo ID
  • Hours: Call Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office for the current schedule
  • Dress code: Facilities restrict clothing that resembles uniforms
  • Video visits: Many jails offer remote options — ask when you call
  • Children: Minors usually need an accompanying adult

What to Expect After Arrest in Salt Lake County

Typical steps after arrest in Salt Lake County:

  1. Booking — fingerprints, photo, property inventory
  2. Medical screening — before general population housing
  3. Classification — housing based on charges and history
  4. Arraignment — first court appearance; bail often set here
  5. Transfer — serious cases may move to a state facility

Frequently Asked Questions — Salt Lake County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Salt Lake County jail?

Start with the official Salt Lake County inmate roster. You can also call Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office at (385) 468-4600. Online records often lag booking by a few hours.

What is the phone number for Salt Lake County Metro Jail?

Contact Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office at (385) 468-4600. Facility address on file: 3415 S 900 W, South Salt Lake, UT 84119.

How long does booking take in Salt Lake County?

Booking commonly takes 2–8 hours depending on volume at Salt Lake County Metro Jail. Weekends and holidays can delay when a name appears in any published system. If urgent, call the facility directly rather than waiting on a website refresh.

Can I visit an inmate at Salt Lake County jail?

Usually yes if the person is eligible and the facility is accepting visits. The main facility listed is Salt Lake County Metro Jail at 3415 S 900 W, South Salt Lake, UT 84119. Bring government photo ID and confirm hours and dress code with Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office before you go. Video visitation may be offered.

What if the person is not listed in the county system?

They may have been released, transferred, or booked under a different name spelling. Check Utah Department of Corrections and the Federal BOP locator for federal custody. Then call Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office to confirm.

How do I send money to someone at Salt Lake County Metro Jail?

Ask Salt Lake County Metro Jail which commissary vendor they use (often JPay, Securus, or Access Corrections) when you call (385) 468-4600. Limits and fees vary by facility — confirm before sending money.
